title: Service interruption concise explainer and technical addendum for customers
body:
Purpose
This draft is intended to serve as a short, customer-facing status update plus a technical addendum for customers who want more detail. Use the top-level snippets for the public status page and the addendum for technical contact/support teams.

High-level public summary (for status.redwood.com and emailed subscribers)
Short headline: Degraded response times and intermittent failures for text generation in US and EU regions — partially mitigated.
What happened (2–3 sentences): On 2027-02-14 at ~03:20 UTC we observed elevated token-latency and intermittent 5xx errors affecting text generation endpoints for a subset of hosted API customers in US-West, US-East, and EU-West. We identified a mis-scheduled routing change combined with an overloaded fallback model pool that caused request queuing beyond SLOs. We applied staged routing rollbacks and capacity rebalancing; by 08:10 UTC the majority of traffic was processed within SLOs with residual tail latency for some long-sequence requests.
Who was affected: Hosted API customers in US and EU regions (approx 0.7% of overall request volume). Dedicated customers using pinned-only model variants were not impacted; Private deployments are unaffected unless they rely on Redwood-managed routing.
Customer impact: Higher-than-normal latency (median +150–400ms; p95 increased to 2.4s for some routes) and intermittent 5xx errors for generation requests. No inference content loss or data exfiltration.
Current status: Primary mitigation applied; monitoring shows reduced error rate and improving latency but continued observation required for long-context workloads.
ETA for full recovery: Monitoring only — full return to baseline expected within 24–48 hours as background cache rehydration and autoscale buffers complete.

Short status snippets (pick one for the status page update)
- "Mitigation deployed — most customers now within normal latency. We continue to monitor for residual tail latency."
- "We identified and rolled back a routing change; affected customers should see improved response times. Ongoing monitoring in place."

Technical addendum (for technical contacts and SREs at customers)
Timeline (UTC, condensed):
- 2027-02-14 03:18: first alert from canary latency monitors (US-West)
- 03:20–03:40: error rate increases on generation endpoints; automated fallback to compatible model variants begins
- 03:45: investigation shows fallback pool reached saturation due to queued requests with large context windows (>= 8k tokens) and cache-miss spike
- 04:05: engineering triggers staged routing rollback to previous policy; emergency autoscale invoked for fallback pool
- 05:10: partial recovery observed in US-West; EU routing still shows elevated queue depth due to cross-region routing propagation delay
- 07:50: additional capacity added and explicit KV-cache prewarming executed for hot prefixes; error rates drop to baseline by 08:10
- 08:10 onward: monitoring shows improving p50/p95; final verification period ongoing

Root cause (summary):
Two factors combined to create the outage window: (1) an automated routing policy change intended to route low-latency requests to a new pool was scheduled but incorrectly applied to a broader set of traffic, including long-sequence generation requests; (2) the fallback model pool (smaller, quantized variants optimized for cost) became oversubscribed because the misapplied routing sent additional long-context workload it was not dimensioned for. The fallback pool’s KV cache saw a cache-miss spiral that reduced its amortized throughput and amplified queuing.

Why this produced customer-visible errors:
- Requests accumulated behind the saturated fallback pool and waited longer than our latency SLOs, causing timeouts and 5xx responses from the proxy layer.
- Long-sequence requests amplified CPU/GPU kernel contention on the fallback nodes because quantized kernels have different memory/latency characteristics for high sequence lengths.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Rolled back the unintended routing change and restored the prior routing policy across affected regions (staged to avoid global disruption).
- Proactively added capacity to fallback pools and triggered accelerated autoscale policies for long-context lanes.
- Manually prewarmed KV caches for high-frequency prefixes observed in the spike window.
- Temporarily expanded the acceptable model-variant compatibility matrix to allow safe local fallbacks within customer’s pinned constraints for eligible hosted traffic.

Customer impact breakdown by product surface:
- Hosted API: impacted (partial) — see timeline above. Customers on free/low-tier plans experienced rate-limited fallback sooner; committed/dedicated customers with reserved pools were largely unaffected.
- Dedicated: not impacted (reserved capacity and pinned pools remained healthy).
- Private: not impacted unless configured to use Redwood-managed routing; if you are unsure, contact your account engineer.

Customer recommended actions (if you saw increased latency or errors):
1) Retry hardened: implement idempotent retry with exponential backoff for generation requests; avoid immediate tight loops for long-sequence retries.
2) Adjust timeouts temporarily: if your application has short per-request timeouts (<= 1s), increase to 4–6s while we finish recovery for long-context workloads.
3) Use model pinning for critical routes: if you require guaranteed latency during platform incidents, consider Dedicated or pin a fast-variant model in hosted with agreed rollout window.
4) Contact support with request IDs: include a few request_ids (from response headers) and timestamps so we can correlate logs faster.

Plans to prevent recurrence (engineering roadmap items):
- Routing change safety: add a preflight dry-run and a stricter traffic-scoping guard for policy changes (canary must be <=0.1% and explicitly marked for long-context-excluded).
- Fallback pool sizing: increase headroom for fallback pools and create a dynamic long-sequence lane that auto-scales differently from short-context lanes.
- Cache resilience: implement a backpressure-aware cache refill policy so a cache-miss spike cannot turn into a cache-miss spiral; add metrics to detect cascading cache-miss amplifications.
- Model-variant compatibility: enforce a rollout checklist that requires verified sequence-length benchmarks for any model variant that will be included in automatic fallback matrices.
- Chaos and pre-mortem exercises: incorporate targeted chaos tests that simulate cross-region routing flips and quantized-model long-sequence stress.

Compensation and SLA note:
Customers eligible for SLA credits will be evaluated per existing SLA terms. If you believe you were materially impacted and need a credits assessment, file a support request with the top-level incident ID and examples of affected requests.

Support contacts and escalation paths:
- For urgent production impact: open a P1 via support.redwood.ai or contact your account engineering Slack channel (if provisioned).
- For technical follow-up: attach 3–5 example request_ids, approximate timestamps (UTC), the route/model used, and a short description of user-visible effect.

Sample customer-facing status update (ready to paste)
Title: Degraded generation performance in US/EU — mitigation in progress
Body: We identified a routing misconfiguration that temporarily directed long-sequence generation traffic to a smaller fallback pool, causing queuing and intermittent failures for a subset of hosted customers. We rolled back the change, added capacity, and prewarmed caches. Most customers are now seeing normal response times; we continue to monitor. We will publish a full post-incident summary once our RCA is complete.

Notes for comms owner
- Use the short status snippet on the public status page first, then send an email to affected customers using the recommended sample update.
- Prepare a follow-up targeted message for enterprise customers that includes specific request examples and any SLA next steps.
- Coordinate with product and SRE for the final RCA; include timeline and list of concrete engineering follow-ups in the final postmortem.

Open questions / follow-up items
- Confirm exact list of affected customers (billing vs. routing intersection) — ownership: CS data team
- Verify fallback-pool quota increase timeline and whether any dedicated customers were temporarily routed — ownership: serving-runtime
- Confirm final metric deltas for p50/p95/p99 for top-10 affected routes — ownership: observability

End of draft

(Prepared by: Aisha Kapoor, Customer Success — draft for internal review before publishing.)
